mainTopic: The wealth taken from מצרים, the time for the morning שמע, and joining גאולה to תפלה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching: the Jews were asked to take the wealth of מצרים so that אברהם would see both halves of the promise come true. רבי אמי and ריש לקיש describe how completely מצרים was emptied. The גמרא then explains doubled words in פסוקים: the double אהיה said to משה, and the double עננו in אליהו's prayer. Next comes the משנה on the morning שמע: it starts when there is enough light to tell תכלת from white, and it ends at sunrise, or three hours into the day according to רבי יהושע. The גמרא explains that the משנה means the strings of ציצית. A ברייתא adds more signs, and the הלכה follows אחרים, while אביי says that for שמע it is best to follow the ותיקין, who finished right at sunrise. This leads to praise of joining גאולה to תפלה, and to the question of how the verses said before and after the עמידה fit with that. The amud ends by showing that the first two chapters of תהלים count as one, and a further proof from רבי יוחנן begins on the next amud.

steps.title: So that אברהם will not say only half the promise came true
steps.stepSummary: The reason for asking the Jews to take wealth is so that אברהם will not say that the slavery came true but the riches did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: That righteous man, אברהם, should not say: 'They will be enslaved and afflicted' was kept for them, but 'and afterward they will leave with great wealth' was not kept for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began earlier. It explains why הקב״ה wanted the Jews to take wealth out of מצרים: so that אברהם would not complain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the ברית בין הבתרים, אברהם was promised two things: slavery, and then leaving with great wealth. If only the slavery came true, the promise would look half-kept. That is why the Jews had to take the riches.

phrases.english: That righteous man
phrases.notes: This is אברהם. The words 'so that he should not say' come just before this line.

phrases.english: "And they will enslave them and afflict them": He kept this for them
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:13

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל״ — לֹא קִייֵּם בָּהֶם.
phrases.english: "And afterward they will leave with great wealth": He did not keep this for them.
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק, וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם קִייֵּם בָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement that started before this section, explaining הקב״ה's request to משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Jews had to take wealth so that both halves of the promise to אברהם would come true.

steps.title: The Jews just want to get out, shown by the parable of the prisoner
steps.stepSummary: The Jews answer that they only want to leave, like a prisoner who would rather go free today with nothing than tomorrow with a lot of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If only we could just get out ourselves! A parable: a man was locked in prison. People told him, 'Tomorrow we will let you out and give you lots of money.' He answered, 'Please, let me out today, and I don't want anything.'
steps.whatsHappening: The Jews answer משה's request. They say they don't care about the money; they just want to leave. A parable shows how they felt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why הקב״ה had to say 'please' in the request. The Jews wanted freedom right away more than they wanted riches later. Like a prisoner, getting out now mattered more than any reward.

phrases.english: They said to him: If only we could get out ourselves!
phrases.notes: 'They' are the Jews and 'him' is משה. 'Ourselves' means just us, with nothing extra.

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל: לְאָדָם שֶׁהָיָה חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים
phrases.english: A parable: to a man who was locked up in prison
and people were saying to him:
We will take you out of prison tomorrow,
and we will give you a lot of money.
And he says to them: Please, I beg you,
take me out today, and I don't ask for anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וּלְוַאי שֶׁנֵּצֵא בְּעַצְמֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The Jews' reply to the request explained in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Jews preferred to leave right away with nothing rather than wait for riches.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the wealth was given against someone's will
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי reads וישאלום as 'they gave against their will'. Two opinions argue about whose will is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they lent them' (וישאלום): רבי אמי said this teaches that they gave it to them against their will. Some say it was against the will of the Egyptians. Some say it was against the will of the Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a פסוק about the Egyptians handing over their valuables. רבי אמי says it happened 'against their will', and then two opinions argue about whose will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word וישאלום is read to mean the giving was forced. But the phrase 'against their will' could point to either side. That is why two opinions appear. The next steps give each side's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And they lent them / gave them what they asked for

phrases.english: "And they lent them": רבי אמי said:
phrases.notes: שמות 12:36

phrases.english: This teaches that they gave it to them against their will.
Some say: against the will of the Egyptians,
and some say: against the will of the Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיַּשְׁאִלוּם, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִשְׁאִילוּם בְּעַל כָּרְחָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how the wealth was actually handed over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The valuables were given against someone's will. Whether that means the Egyptians or the Jews is argued.

steps.title: Reason for 'against the Egyptians' will': the wealth was שלל
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that it was against the Egyptians' will brings a פסוק calling the wealth 'שלל', spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it was against the will of the Egyptians: because it is written, 'And she who stays at home divides the spoils.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the first opinion. A פסוק in תהלים calls the wealth 'spoils'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spoils are taken from an enemy who does not want to give them. So if the wealth of מצרים is called שלל, the Egyptians must have handed it over unwillingly.

phrases.english: The one who says: against the will of the Egyptians
because it is written: "And she who stays at home divides the spoils."
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:13. Spoils are taken from an enemy who doesn't want to give them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּמִצְרַיִם דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the first opinion in step 3.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 68:13, which calls the wealth שלל

steps.title: Reason for 'against the Jews' will': the heavy load
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that it was against the Jews' will explains that the Jews did not want to carry heavy loads on the journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it was against the will of the Jews: because of the load.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the second opinion: the Jews did not want the extra weight to carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits step 2: the Jews just wanted to get out. Carrying heavy valuables on a long trip was a burden, so they took them only because they were told to.

keyTerms.meaning: A load, a burden to carry

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי says the wealth was given 'against their will'. One opinion says the Egyptians were unwilling, because the wealth is called שלל. The other says the Jews were unwilling, because of the heavy load.

phrases.english: The one who says: against the will of the Jews
because of the load.
phrases.notes: He means they didn't want heavy things to carry on the long trip out of מצרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעַל כָּרְחָם דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִשּׁוּם מַשּׂוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the second opinion in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the Jews took the wealth unwillingly
steps.raayaSupportSource: Common sense: heavy loads are a burden on a journey

steps.title: רבי אמי: מצרים was left like a trap with no grain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains ויינצלו את מצרים: the Jews left מצרים as empty as a bird trap with no bait.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they emptied Egypt." רבי אמי said: this teaches that they made it like a trap with no grain in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same פסוק about the Jews taking the Egyptians' wealth. רבי אמי gives a picture of how completely empty מצרים was left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird trap works because of the grain left inside as bait. Once the grain is gone, the trap is useless and empty. So מצרים was left with nothing of value.

phrases.english: "And they emptied Egypt."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:36

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
This teaches that they made it like a trap
that has no grain in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק about the wealth taken from מצרים, now explaining the word ויינצלו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצרים was left as empty as a bird trap with no grain.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: מצרים was left like a sea with no fish
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different picture: מצרים was left like deep water with no fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: they made it like the deep sea with no fish in it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers his own picture for the same word, ויינצלו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that מצרים was totally emptied. They only use different images: an empty trap, or deep water with no fish.

keyTerms.meaning: the deep part of the sea

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
They made it like the deep sea
that has no fish in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר, עֲשָׂאוּהָ כִּמְצוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second image for the same word that רבי אמי explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצרים was left like deep water emptied of fish.
steps.whatToRemember: Both images say the same thing: the Jews left מצרים completely emptied of its wealth, so the promise to אברהם of great riches came true.

steps.title: The double 'I will be': with you now and in future exiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why אהיה is said twice: הקדוש ברוך הוא was with Israel in this slavery and will be with them in future slavery under the kingdoms.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I will be that I will be." הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: Go tell Israel, I was with you in this slavery, and I will be with you in the slavery under the kingdoms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק that repeats a word, אהיה, and explains what each one means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first אהיה refers to the current slavery in מצרים, and the second points to future exiles under other nations. The message is that ה׳ stays with Israel in every exile.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be that I will be (a name of ה׳ told to משה)
kingdoms (the later nations that would rule over Israel)
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: "I will be that I will be."
phrases.notes: שמות 3:14

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Go tell Israel:
I was with you in this slavery,
and I will be with you in the slavery under the kingdoms.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה״, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a double word in the פסוק at the burning bush.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double אהיה means: I am with you in this exile and will be with you in future exiles.

steps.title: משה objects: don't tell them about future suffering now
steps.stepSummary: משה argues that it is enough to deal with each trouble when it comes, so there is no need to mention future exiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said before Him: Master of the World, a trouble is enough in its own time.
steps.whatsHappening: משה pushes back on the message he was told to deliver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people are already suffering in מצרים. Telling them now about future exiles would only add pain, so משה asks to leave that part out.

keyTerms.meaning: a trouble is enough in its own time

phrases.english: He said before Him:
phrases.notes: "He" is משה.

phrases.english: Master of the World,
a trouble is enough in its own time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, דַּיָּה לַצָּרָה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה objects to the second half of the message in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The instruction to tell Israel about future slavery under the kingdoms.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning future suffering to people already suffering adds pain and is not needed now.

steps.title: ה׳ agrees: say only 'I will be has sent me'
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא accepts משה's point and tells him to say only one אהיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: Go tell them, "I will be has sent me to you."
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ agrees with משה and shortens the message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the end of the same פסוק says only one אהיה. The part about future exiles was not given to the people.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be has sent me to you

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Go tell them:
"I will be has sent me to you."
phrases.notes: Notice there is just one אהיה here. The part about the future was dropped.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: לֵךְ אֱמוֹר לָהֶם ״אֶהְיֶה שְׁלָחַנִי אֲלֵיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves משה's objection by agreeing with it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The people were told only one אהיה; the future exiles were not mentioned to them.
steps.whatToRemember: The first half of the פסוק has a double אהיה for משה, and the second half has a single אהיה for the people, because ה׳ agreed not to burden them with future suffering.

steps.title: Why did אליהו say 'answer me' twice?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks why אליהו repeated the word עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Answer me, ה׳, answer me." רבי אבהו said: Why did אליהו say "answer me" two times?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק with a repeated word and asks why. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said "answer me" just once. The repetition suggests אליהו was asking for two separate things.

phrases.english: "Answer me, ה׳, answer me."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:37

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Why did Eliyahu say
"answer me" two times?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָה אָמַר אֵלִיָּהוּ עֲנֵנִי שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another example of a doubled word in a פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the repeated word עננו.

steps.title: Two requests: fire from heaven, and no claims of sorcery
steps.stepSummary: The first עננו asks for fire to come down; the second asks that the people not explain the miracle away as כישוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that אליהו said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World, answer me, that fire should come down from heaven and consume everything on the altar. And answer me, that You turn their minds away, so they will not say it was sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that each עננו was a separate request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miracle alone was not enough, because the people might call it magic. So אליהו asked for a second thing: that their minds not go to that explanation, so the miracle would actually bring them back to ה׳.

phrases.english: This teaches that Eliyahu said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
"Answer me": that fire should come down from heaven
and consume everything that is on the altar,
and "answer me": that You turn their minds away,
so that they will not say
they are acts of sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָמַר אֵלִיָּהוּ לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first עננו is for fire from heaven; the second is that the people not call it sorcery.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The end of the same פסוק, "You turned their heart backward," shows that אליהו asked ה׳ to act on the people's minds.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And You turned their heart backward."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the second request from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words about ה׳ turning their heart show that אליהו's prayer was also about the people's thinking, not only about the fire. This backs up the second meaning of עננו.

phrases.english: As it says:
"And You turned their heart backward."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, מלכים א 18:37.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה הֲסִבֹּתָ אֶת לִבָּם אֲחוֹרַנִּית״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second request explained in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That אליהו's second request was about the people's minds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of מלכים א 18:37, "ואתה הסבת את לבם אחורנית".
steps.whatToRemember: אליהו's double עננו means two requests: a real miracle, and that the people accept it as coming from ה׳ instead of calling it magic.

steps.title: The earliest time for the morning שמע
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the morning שמע may begin once a person can tell תכלת from white. רבי אליעזר says the sign is telling תכלת from leek-green.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From when may one say שמע in the morning? From when a person can tell sky-blue from white. רבי אליעזר says: from when he can tell sky-blue from leek-green.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, and its first question is when the morning שמע may start. Two opinions give a sign based on how much light there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign for 'morning' here is not a clock time. It is the point when there is enough light to see a color difference. Leek-green is much closer to blue than white is, so רבי אליעזר's test needs more light and starts a little later.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the text the גמרא is about to discuss)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
From when does one recite שמע in the morning?
From when one can tell apart sky-blue and white.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Between sky-blue and leek-green.
phrases.notes: Read it as: from when one can tell these two apart. Those words carry over from the line before.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאֵימָתַי קוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע בְּשַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, still in the first perek, after the aggadic material on אהיה and אליהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The morning שמע begins when one can tell תכלת from white; רבי אליעזר says from when one can tell תכלת from leek-green.

steps.title: The latest time for the morning שמע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's statement continues: one must finish by sunrise. רבי יהושע says until three hours into the day, because kings get up then.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must finish it by sunrise. רבי יהושע says: until three hours into the day, because that is when kings get up.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the end of the time window for the morning שמע. There are two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea underneath is that שמע is said 'when you rise'. The question is how late 'rising time' lasts. רבי יהושע points out that some people, like kings, get up as late as three hours into the day, so rising time stretches that far.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunrise, when the sun starts to shine

phrases.english: And one finishes it by sunrise.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: until three hours,
for such is the way of kings
to get up at three hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגוֹמְרָהּ עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the start time, the משנה gives the end time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: finish by הנץ החמה. רבי יהושע: until three hours into the day, the time kings rise.

steps.title: Reading after the time still has value
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says שמע after the time has not lost out completely. He is like a person reading from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who reads it after this time has not lost out. He is like a person reading in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by telling us what happens if a person says שמע too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the time, he no longer does the מצוה of קריאת שמע at its proper time. But the words are still Torah, so he still gets credit for learning Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Has not lost out' does not mean he did the מצוה of שמע on time. It means he still has the reward of reading Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: The morning שמע starts with enough light to tell colors apart and ends at sunrise or at three hours. After that, saying it counts like reading Torah.

phrases.english: One who reads from this point onward
has not lost out,
like a person reading in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹרֵא מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ לֹא הִפְסִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happens after the end time set in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע after the time is not a total loss; it counts like reading Torah.

steps.title: What does 'תכלת and white' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by telling apart תכלת and white.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'between sky-blue and white' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what the משנה's first sign means. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say what objects are being compared. The גמרא wants to know exactly what a person is supposed to look at.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is 'between sky-blue and white'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְלָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first sign in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which blue and white objects the משנה means.

steps.title: It cannot mean two piles of wool
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests it means a pile of white wool and a pile of blue wool. It rejects this, because those are easy to tell apart even at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a pile of white wool and a pile of blue wool, people can tell those apart even at night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a possible answer and pushes it away right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is supposed to mark the start of the day. Two large piles of different colors can be told apart even in the dark. A test that works at night cannot be a sign that day has come.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggested answer about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say
between a pile of white wool
and a pile of sky-blue wool,
but at night too, people can tell them apart!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בֵּין גְּבָבָא דְעַמְרָא חִיוָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers one possible answer to the question and knocks it down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the משנה means separate piles of white and blue wool.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such piles can be told apart even at night, so they cannot mark the start of the day.

steps.title: It means the blue and white strings of ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה means the blue strings and the white strings that are together on the ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the blue strings in it and the white strings in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ציצית the blue and white strings are thin and twisted close together. Telling them apart takes real daylight, so this works as a sign that morning has come.

phrases.english: Rather,
between the sky-blue in it and the white in it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the ציצית. The גמרא doesn't say the word, but it's talking about the strings on one garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת שֶׁבָּהּ לְלָבָן שֶׁבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected wool-pile reading with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sign is telling apart the blue and white strings of the same ציצית.
steps.whatToRemember: 'תכלת and white' means the strings of ציצית side by side, not separate piles of wool.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives three more signs for morning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three more opinions. רבי מאיר: telling a wolf from a dog. רבי עקיבא: telling a donkey from a wild donkey. אחרים: seeing a friend four אמות away and recognizing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says: from when one can tell a wolf from a dog. רבי עקיבא says: a donkey from a wild donkey. אחרים say: from when one can see his friend four אמות away and recognize him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more opinions on when the morning שמע may begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion uses a different test for 'enough light'. The animal pairs look alike, so they need good light to tell apart. אחרים use recognizing a person a short distance away.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Meir says:
From when one can tell apart a wolf and a dog.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בֵּין חֲמוֹר לְעָרוֹד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: between a donkey and a wild donkey.
And others say:

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁיִּרְאֶה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ רָחוֹק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, וְיַכִּירֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: From when he sees his friend four cubits away and recognizes him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר מִשֶּׁיַּכִּיר בֵּין זְאֵב לְכֶלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's start-time question and adds opinions from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning begins at a wolf/dog distinction (רבי מאיר), a donkey/wild donkey distinction (רבי עקיבא), or recognizing a friend at four אמות (אחרים).

steps.title: רב הונא rules like אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה follows אחרים: the morning time starts when you can recognize a friend from four אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: After the list of opinions in the ברייתא, רב הונא decides which opinion is the halacha. He picks אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 listed several signs for when morning starts. אחרים gave the sign of recognizing a friend at four אמות. רב הונא makes that the practical rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'others'; a תנא quoted without his name

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha is like Acherim.
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from step 20: recognizing a friend four אמות away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the opinions brought in the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows אחרים: the morning time begins when one can recognize a friend at four אמות.

steps.title: אביי splits the ruling: תפילין versus קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ruling of אחרים applies to תפילין. For קריאת שמע one should follow the ותיקין, who, as רבי יוחנן reports, finished שמע exactly at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For תפילין, follow אחרים. For קריאת שמע, follow the ותיקין. As רבי יוחנן said: The ותיקין used to finish it right at sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב הונא's ruling. אחרים sets the time for putting on תפילין, but for שמע the best practice is that of the ותיקין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gives each מצוה its own guideline. תפילין may be put on from the time of אחרים. For שמע, אביי points to the practice of the ותיקין, and רבי יוחנן explains what that was: they timed שמע so they finished right as the sun came up.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, a מצוה done in the daytime
Sunrise, when the sun first appears

steps.confusionAlert: The ותיקין are not setting the earliest allowed time for שמע. They describe the ideal way to do it: finishing exactly at sunrise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice of davening ותיקין, saying שמע so it ends at sunrise.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For tefillin, like Acherim.
phrases.notes: In other words, you may put on תפילין once you can recognize a friend at four אמות.

phrases.english: For the reading of Shema, like the vatikin.
As Rabbi Yochanan said:
The vatikin would finish it
phrases.notes: 'It' means קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: together with sunrise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לִתְפִילִּין כַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's ruling to תפילין and gives a separate guideline for שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tefillin follow אחרים. For קריאת שמע one should follow the ותיקין and finish at sunrise.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ותיקין and explains their reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says the ותיקין finished שמע at sunrise. Their reason was to go straight from the ברכה of גאולה into תפלה, and so pray in the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: The ותיקין used to finish it at sunrise, so that they would connect גאולה to תפלה, and end up praying in the daytime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן. It also adds the reason behind the practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after שמע comes the ברכה about redemption, which ends 'גאל ישראל'. Finishing at sunrise lets a person go straight from that ברכה into שמונה עשרה with no break. It also means the שמונה עשרה itself starts after sunrise, in real daytime.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way': a ברייתא that supports what was just said
Redemption; here the ברכה after שמע ending 'גאל ישראל'
To join, to place right next to

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
The vatikin would finish it
together with sunrise,
so that he would join redemption to prayer,
phrases.notes: That means going straight from the ברכה 'גאל ישראל' into שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: and so he ends up praying in the daytime.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's report from a ברייתא and adds the reason.
steps.raayaObject: That the ותיקין finished שמע at sunrise
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that also gives the reason: joining גאולה to תפלה and praying in the daytime

steps.title: רבי זירא gives a פסוק for the practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא shows the ותיקין's practice is hinted at in a פסוק: 'They shall fear You with the sun.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is the פסוק for this? 'They shall fear You with the sun, and before the moon, for all generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks where in תנ"ך the ותיקין's practice comes from, and answers with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With the sun' is read as showing fear of Heaven right when the sun rises. So accepting Heaven's authority through שמע and then davening should line up with sunrise.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק for this?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
What is the verse for this?
"They shall fear You with the sun,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:5

phrases.english: "and before the moon, for all generations."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the ותיקין practice described in steps 22-23.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of the ותיקין to say שמע and daven at sunrise
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 72:5: 'They shall fear You with the sun'

steps.title: Joining גאולה to תפלה protects a person all day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן אליקים reports in the name of the holy community of ירושלים that someone who joins גאולה to תפלה will not be harmed that whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן אליקים testified in the name of the holy community in ירושלים: Anyone who joins גאולה to תפלה will not be harmed the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a statement about the reward for going straight from the ברכה of גאולה into שמונה עשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 gave joining גאולה to תפלה as the reason for the ותיקין's timing. Now we learn how valuable that joining is: it brings protection for the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy community in ירושלים, a known group of חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to finish שמע at sunrise and go straight from 'גאל ישראל' into שמונה עשרה. This joining of גאולה to תפלה is very valuable and brings protection all day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a main source for the rule not to break between 'גאל ישראל' and שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Elyakim testified
in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:
Anyone who joins redemption to prayer
will not be harmed the whole day.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דְבִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea of joining גאולה to תפלה from step 23 and adds its reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever joins גאולה to תפלה will not be harmed the entire day.

steps.title: רבי זירא says he joined them and was still harmed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges the promise from step 25. He joined גאולה to תפלה and was still harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Is that really true? I joined them, and I was still harmed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on the promise that joining גאולה to תפלה protects a person all day. He uses his own life as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 promised no harm the whole day. רבי זירא says he did exactly this and something bad still happened to him. So either the promise is wrong, or his 'harm' needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (an expression of doubt)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Is that so?!
But I joined [them], and I was harmed!
phrases.notes: He means joining גאולה to תפלה, the practice praised in step 25.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אֲנָא סְמַכִי וְאִיתְּזַקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the promise of step 25 using personal experience.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one who joins גאולה to תפלה is not harmed all day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real counter-example: רבי זירא did it and was harmed anyway.

steps.title: Bringing a gift to the king was not real harm
steps.stepSummary: He is answered that his 'harm' was having to bring myrtle to the king's palace. That was really a privilege worth paying for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What harm did you suffer? That you had to bring myrtle to the king's palace? You should have been willing to pay money for the chance to see the king's face!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא's challenge is answered by reframing his 'harm'. What he thought was a burden was actually an honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'harm' was a duty to bring a myrtle gift to the king. The answer says people should pay for the chance to see a king, so this was a gain, not a loss. The promise of step 25 stays intact.

phrases.english: He said to him: In what way were you harmed?
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יוסי בן אליקים, who gave the promise in step 25.

phrases.english: That you brought myrtle to the king's palace?
There too, you should have been ready
to pay a fee to see the face of the king,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּמַאי אִיתְּזַקְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by redefining the 'harm'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the event: what looked like harm was actually a benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Having to bring a gift to the king was a harm, which would disprove the promise.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeing a king is a privilege worth paying for, so no real harm happened.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: run to see kings, even non-Jewish ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's teaching proves that seeing a king is valuable. One should run to see even non-Jewish kings, so that one can later see the difference when the kings of Israel return.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: A person should always try to run to greet the kings of Israel. And not only the kings of Israel, but even the kings of the nations, so that if he merits, he will see the difference between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer in step 27. רבי יוחנן teaches that seeing a king, even a non-Jewish one, is worth the effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 claimed that seeing a king is worth paying for. רבי יוחנן's teaching backs this up, even for non-Jewish kings, because it lets a person compare them later to the kings of Israel. So רבי זירא's trip to the king was a real gain.

keyTerms.meaning: should make an effort, try hard
kings of the nations of the world
he will distinguish, see the difference

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's 'harm' was really a privilege, so the promise for joining גאולה to תפלה still stands.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person should always make an effort
to run to greet the kings of Israel.
And not only to greet the kings of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לִקְרַאת מַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: but even to greet the kings of the nations of the world,
so that if he merits, he will be able to tell the difference
phrases.notes: He means: if he merits to live to see the גאולה.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם!
phrases.english: between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations of the world!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְעוֹלָם יִשְׁתַּדֵּל אָדָם לָרוּץ לִקְרַאת מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 27 that seeing a king is worth paying for.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that seeing a king's face is a privilege.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching that one should run to greet kings, even non-Jewish ones.

steps.title: רבי אלעא asks עולא to honor his brother רב ברונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעא asks עולא to greet his brother רב ברונא publicly in בבל, because he is a great man who rejoices in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעא said to עולא: When you go there, ask about the welfare of my brother רב ברונא in front of the whole group, because he is a great man and he rejoices in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. רבי אלעא asks עולא to honor רב ברונא in public, and this sets up the next step, which shows how much he rejoiced in מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greeting someone in front of everyone shows him respect. רבי אלעא gives two reasons: רב ברונא is a great man, and he is joyful about מצוות. The next step gives an example connected to joining גאולה to תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: ask after the welfare of, greet
in the presence of the whole group

phrases.english: Rabbi El'a said to Ulla:
When you go there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means בבל, where עולא was traveling.

phrases.english: ask after the welfare of my brother, Rav Beruna,
in the presence of the whole group,
because he is a great man and rejoices in מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אִלָּעָא לְעוּלָּא: כִּי עָיְילַתְּ לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story, which will connect to joining גאולה to תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ברונא deserves public honor because he is great and rejoices in מצוות.

steps.title: רב ברונא joined them and was joyful all day
steps.stepSummary: Proof that רב ברונא rejoiced in מצוות: once he joined גאולה to תפלה, and he could not stop laughing with joy the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One time he joined גאולה to תפלה, and laughter did not leave his mouth the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב ברונא really did rejoice in מצוות. He was so happy after joining גאולה to תפלה that he was laughing all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רבי אלעא's praise from step 29. It also ties back to the theme of steps 22-25: joining גאולה to תפלה, the way the ותיקין did, is a special accomplishment.

phrases.english: Once he joined redemption to prayer,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא פְּסֵיק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵּיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא.
phrases.english: and laughter did not stop from his mouth the whole day.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנָא חֲדָא סְמַךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the example proving the praise in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That רב ברונא rejoices in מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of his joy all day after joining גאולה to תפלה.

steps.title: How can you join them if a verse is said in between?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how joining גאולה to תפלה is possible, since רבי יוחנן says to recite 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' at the start of the תפלה, which seems to separate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can a person join them? But רבי יוחנן said: At the beginning one says 'ה׳ open my lips', and at the end one says 'May the words of my mouth be acceptable'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole idea of joining גאולה to תפלה. If an extra verse is said before the תפלה, then the two are not really joined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining means nothing comes between the ברכה of גאולה and the תפלה. רבי יוחנן's rule puts the verse 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' right before the תפלה, so it looks like an interruption. The verse said at the end is mentioned to show the full pattern, but the problem is only the verse at the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'ה׳, open my lips', the verse said before the תפלה
'May they be acceptable', the verse said after the תפלה

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the verse at the end. Only 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח', said between גאולה and the תפלה, creates the problem of an interruption.

phrases.english: How is one able to join [them]?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
At the beginning one says: "Lord, open my lips,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:17

phrases.english: and at the end one says:
"May the words of my mouth be acceptable, etc."!
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:15

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי מָצֵי סָמֵיךְ? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the halachic question of whether joining גאולה to תפלה is possible at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of joining גאולה to תפלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן requires a verse before the תפלה, which seems to interrupt between גאולה and תפלה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: that verse is for the evening prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that רבי יוחנן's rule about saying 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' first applies to ערבית, so in the morning nothing interrupts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Let it apply to the evening prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question of step 31. He limits רבי יוחנן's rule to the evening prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is said only at ערבית, then in שחרית nothing comes between גאולה and תפלה. That way the morning joining of the ותיקין still works.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Let it be in the evening prayer.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's rule about saying 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' first is for ערבית, not the morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: תְּהֵא בִּתְפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by limiting רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the rule applies to a different prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is said before every תפלה, including שחרית, so it interrupts the joining.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is said at ערבית, so the morning joining of גאולה to תפלה is not interrupted.

steps.title: Joining גאולה to תפלה matters at ערבית too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's answer. רבי יוחנן himself says that one who joins גאולה to תפלה at ערבית earns עולם הבא, so 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' should not interrupt there either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: Who is a person of the World to Come? The one who joins the גאולה of ערבית to the תפלה of ערבית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 32. Moving 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' to ערבית does not help, because at ערבית we also want to join גאולה to תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר thought the verse could go at ערבית without causing a problem. But רבי יוחנן praises joining גאולה to תפלה specifically at ערבית. If the verse interrupts there, it breaks something רבי יוחנן values very highly. So the answer of Step 32 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has a share in the World to Come
The one who joins / places right next to
The ברכה after שמע that ends 'גאל ישראל'

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
Who is a person of the World to Come?
It is the one who joins the גאולה of ערבית
to the תפלה of ערבית!
phrases.notes: So the verse can't go before ערבית either, since it would split them there too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's answer that 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' belongs at ערבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן values joining גאולה to תפלה at ערבית too, so placing the verse there causes the same interruption.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר moves the verse to מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר changes his answer. 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is said before מנחה, where no גאולה comes right before the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: Let it be said at the מנחה prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new answer: רבי יוחנן's rule about saying 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is only for מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מנחה there is no שמע and no גאולה before the עמידה. So saying the verse there cannot split anything apart. This keeps both of רבי יוחנן's teachings working without any clash.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not our practice. We say 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' before every עמידה. רב אשי's answer in the next step explains why that is fine.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי אלעזר said:
Let it be at the מנחה prayer.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the verse 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' (תהלים 51:17).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 33 by replacing the answer of Step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the rule applies only to מנחה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is said before ערבית, which would interrupt between גאולה and תפלה at night
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is said only before מנחה, where there is no גאולה to interrupt

steps.title: רב אשי: the verse counts as part of the תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the verse can be said before every תפלה. Since the רבנן made it part of the תפלה, it counts as the start of the תפלה and is not an interruption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say it is said before all the prayers. Since the רבנן set it into the תפלה, it is like a longer תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' can be said before every תפלה, and it still does not interrupt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר limited where the verse is said. רב אשי keeps it everywhere and changes how we view it instead. The verse is not a gap between גאולה and תפלה. It is the opening of the תפלה itself, so גאולה is still joined directly to תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן set it in place
It is like / it is considered

steps.whyThisMatters: This matches our practice. We say 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' before every עמידה, including שחרית right after גאל ישראל.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
You can even say it is on all of them,
phrases.notes: All of them means every תפלה, even שחרית and ערבית.

phrases.english: and since the רבנן set it into the תפלה,
it is like a longer תפלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אַכּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same problem that רבי אלעזר answered in Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the verse as part of the תפלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is an interruption between גאולה and תפלה
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse was set by the רבנן as part of the תפלה, so it is not an interruption

steps.title: Proof from השכיבנו at night
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves his idea. At ערבית we say השכיבנו after גאולה and still count it as joined, because the רבנן made השכיבנו part of the גאולה. The same is true of the verse before the תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, how can one join them at ערבית? He must say 'השכיבנו'! Rather, since the רבנן instituted השכיבנו, it is like a longer גאולה. So too, since the רבנן set the verse into the תפלה, it is like a longer תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a proof for his answer from השכיבנו, the extra ברכה we say at night after גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At ערבית there is always a ברכה, השכיבנו, between גאל ישראל and the עמידה. Yet רבי יוחנן still calls this joining גאולה to תפלה. That only works if a piece set by the רבנן counts as part of what it is attached to. In the same way, 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' counts as part of the תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so
The ברכה after גאולה at night ('Lay us down')

steps.whatToRemember: Something the רבנן built into a prayer counts as part of it. השכיבנו is part of גאולה, and 'ה׳ שפתי תפתח' is part of תפלה, so neither one breaks the joining of גאולה to תפלה.

phrases.english: For if you don't say so,
how can one join them at ערבית?
But he has to say 'השכיבנו'!
phrases.notes: השכיבנו comes after גאל ישראל and before the עמידה, so it seems to sit in between them.

phrases.english: Rather, since the רבנן instituted השכיבנו,
it is like a longer גאולה.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי כֵּיוָן דְּקַבְעוּהָ רַבָּנַן בִּתְפִלָּה —
phrases.english: So too, since the רבנן set it into the תפלה,
it is like a longer תפלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in Step 35
steps.raayaObject: That a piece the רבנן added to a prayer counts as part of that prayer and is not an interruption
steps.raayaSupportSource: השכיבנו at ערבית, which comes between גאולה and תפלה yet still counts as joining them

steps.title: Why is 'May the words of my mouth be acceptable' said at the end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the פסוק 'יהיו לרצון אמרי פי' could refer to the prayer just finished or to the prayer about to be said. So why did the רבנן place it after the שמונה עשרה ברכות and not at the beginning?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, this פסוק 'May the words of my mouth be acceptable' can mean the end of prayer, and it can also mean the beginning, about what I am about to say. So why did the רבנן put it after the eighteen ברכות? Let them say it at the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the פסוק said at the end of the עמידה. It asks why it was placed at the end when it could just as easily open the prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'may my words be acceptable' works both ways. It can be a request about words already said, or about words I am about to say. Since both readings work, the גמרא wants to know why the רבנן chose the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a line of reasoning)
May the words of my mouth be acceptable (תהלים 19:15)
The רבנן set it up (instituted it)

phrases.english: Now, since this verse 'May the words of my mouth be acceptable'
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:15. This is the פסוק we say right after the עמידה.

phrases.english: can mean at the end,
and can mean at the beginning, about what I want to say.
why did the Rabbis institute it
after the eighteen blessings?
Let them say it at the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, הַאי ״יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי״ מַשְׁמַע לִבְסוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the פסוק said before the עמידה (ה׳ שפתי תפתח) to the פסוק said after it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן placed 'יהיו לרצון' after the שמונה עשרה ברכות rather than before them.

steps.title: דוד said it after eighteen chapters
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי explains that דוד wrote this פסוק after eighteen chapters of תהלים. So the רבנן placed it after the eighteen ברכות of the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, said: Since דוד said it only after eighteen chapters, the רבנן placed it after the eighteen ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question. The placement of the פסוק in the עמידה copies its placement in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a parallel. In תהלים the פסוק comes after eighteen chapters. In the עמידה it comes after eighteen ברכות. The order of the prayer follows the order in דוד's book.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
Since David did not say it
except after eighteen chapters,
phrases.notes: He means the chapters of תהלים that come before this פסוק.

phrases.english: therefore the Rabbis instituted it
after the eighteen blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The placement copies תהלים. The פסוק comes after eighteen chapters there, so it comes after eighteen ברכות here.

steps.title: But there are nineteen chapters!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count. The פסוק is at the end of chapter 19 of תהלים, so nineteen chapters come before it, not eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are eighteen?! They are nineteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 38 by checking the numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole parallel depends on the number eighteen. If the פסוק actually closes chapter 19, the count does not match the eighteen ברכות, and the answer seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: These are eighteen?!
They are nineteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה?! תְּשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה הָוְיָן!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count used in step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי's claim that the פסוק comes after eighteen chapters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק ends chapter 19, so nineteen chapters precede it, and the parallel to eighteen ברכות breaks.

steps.title: The first two chapters of תהלים count as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'אשרי האיש' (chapter 1) and 'למה רגשו גוים' (chapter 2) are really one chapter. So only eighteen chapters come before the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Happy is the man' and 'Why are the nations in an uproar' are one chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer of step 38. It shows that the count really is eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our printed books split chapters 1 and 2. The גמרא says they belong together as a single chapter. That makes the count eighteen, and the parallel to the eighteen ברכות works again.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy is the man (opening of תהלים chapter 1)
Why are the nations in an uproar (opening of תהלים chapter 2)

steps.whatToRemember: 'יהיו לרצון' is said after the עמידה because in תהלים it comes after eighteen chapters, when the first two chapters are counted as one.

phrases.english: 'Happy is the man' and 'Why are the nations in an uproar'
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים.

phrases.english: are one chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ״ וְ״לָמָּה רָגְשׁוּ גוֹיִם״ חֲדָא פָּרָשָׁה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recount the chapters: two chapters join into one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים are separate, so there are nineteen chapters.
steps.terutzMaskana: Chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter, so there are eighteen, matching the eighteen ברכות.

steps.title: דוד said 103 chapters before saying הללויה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי says that דוד wrote 103 chapters of תהלים and did not say 'הללויה' until he saw the downfall of the רשעים (תהלים 104:35).
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי said: דוד said 103 chapters, and he did not say 'הללויה' until he saw the downfall of the wicked. As it says: 'Let sinners cease from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless ה׳, my soul, הללויה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement to back up its claim from step 40 that chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים are one chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement says the first 'הללויה' comes at the end of chapter 103. In our printed תהלים that verse is at the end of chapter 104. The statement only fits if two of the earlier chapters are counted as one, and the גמרא will point this out next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Praise God', a word of praise in תהלים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same חכם who counted eighteen chapters in step 38. His counting only works if chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter, so his own words support the answer in step 40.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
phrases.notes: This is the same חכם who gave the 'eighteen chapters' answer back in step 38.

phrases.english: David said one hundred and three chapters,
and he did not say 'Halleluyah'
until he saw the downfall of the wicked,
as it is stated: 'Let sinners cease from the earth
and let the wicked be no more;
bless ה׳, my soul, Halleluyah.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:35

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the step 40 answer that chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'אשרי האיש' and 'למה רגשו גוים' are a single chapter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי's statement that the first 'הללויה' comes after 103 chapters (תהלים 104:35).

steps.title: The count looks like 104, not 103
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that by the normal count, the verse with the first 'הללויה' is in chapter 104, not 103.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these 103? They are 104!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the number in the statement just quoted. By the normal count, there are 104 chapters, not 103.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same counting problem as in step 39, where eighteen seemed to be nineteen. Here 103 seems to be 104. Asking the question sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against step 40. The גמרא raises the counting problem so it can show that only the step 40 answer solves it.

phrases.english: Are these one hundred and three?
They are one hundred and four!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מֵאָה וְשָׁלֹשׁ? מֵאָה וְאַרְבַּע הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the number 103 in the statement just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The number 103 in רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse with the first 'הללויה' is in chapter 104 of our תהלים, so the number 103 seems wrong.

steps.title: So the first two chapters are one chapter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'אשרי האיש' and 'למה רגשו גוים' are one chapter. Then it starts to bring another proof from רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that 'Happy is the man' and 'Why are the nations in uproar' are one chapter. As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the count of 103 only works if chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter. Then it begins to bring a second proof, which continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate counts by this חכם, eighteen and 103, both work only if chapters 1 and 2 are joined. That makes the step 40 answer much stronger. The last line opens another proof from רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude from this
'Happy is the man', the opening of תהלים chapter 1

steps.whatToRemember: תהלים chapters 1 ('אשרי האיש') and 2 ('למה רגשו גוים') count as one chapter. That is why 'יהיו לרצון' comes after eighteen chapters, and the first 'הללויה' comes after 103.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the רבנן placed 'יהיו לרצון אמרי פי' after the eighteen ברכות of the עמידה.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from this
that 'Happy is the man' and 'Why are the nations in uproar'
are one chapter.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem in step 42 and confirms the step 40 answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אשרי האיש' and 'למה רגשו גוים' are a single chapter of תהלים. A further proof from רבי יוחנן begins next.
